question.text: Under Regulation 20(11) of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, the appointment of a custodian for a Category I or Category II AIF is:

answer.text: Mandatory for all AIFs — the Sponsor / Manager shall appoint a custodian for safekeeping of the securities of the fund.
Mandatory only if the corpus exceeds ₹500 crore.
Optional for Cat II AIFs and mandatory only for Cat I.
Required only for AIFs that invest in listed securities.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Regulation 20(11) of the AIF Regulations (as updated), the Sponsor/Manager of AIFs SHALL appoint a custodian for safekeeping of the securities of the fund. Under the existing SEBI regulations, appointing a custodian is MANDATORY for ALL AIFs. Each scheme can have a different custodian to segregate assets and liabilities of each scheme. The Trap: There is no ₹500 crore corpus threshold for custodian appointment. Custodian is mandatory across Cat I, II and III — not optional for Cat II. The listed-securities carve-out was historical and has since been removed. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests custodian mandatoriness identically. Historically Cat III needed a custodian first — now uniform. Manager's Pro-Tip: The Sponsor/Manager must appoint the custodian PRIOR TO the date of first investment of the scheme. Commit to shortlisting custodians 60-90 days ahead of expected first investment, not after first close.
